newsitem.title: CROATIA: Creditanstalt sees Croatia market share.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt sees Croatia market share.

text.p: CAIB d.d., a new Croatian arm of Austria's Creditanstalt-Bankverein investment unit, said on Thursday it would seek a share of the securities business on Croatia's expanding market.
"We are looking for a 20-percent market share. Our target is $100 million turnover a year," director Gabriel Dielacher told Reuters during an international investment conference.
"This is achievable," he said but pointed out that the market with no more than two fully-listed stocks, drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka, was too narrow.

The Croatian unit has been put in charge of expansion on other former Yugoslav markets. Dielacher said CAIB wanted to open a brokerage last spring but decided to hold back and wait for things to pick up on Zagreb's bourse.
Stronger trading in Pliva and Zagrebacka in recent months, following their flotation and listing abroad, has also boosted other issues such as food and hotel stocks.
Daily volume has increased to tens of thousands from perhaps a few hundred shares earlier this year, lifting turnover to over 20 million kuna ($4 million) on most days.
But Dielacher said it would still take between seven and 12 fully-listed companies from different branches to produce the desired trading level and added:
"With a better market structure, volume will also come."

He added that CAIB held an important position on the securities market in neighbouring Slovenia, where it is now making some $20 million per month. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
